extracted.intended_audience: administrators, Title IX coordinators, legal/compliance staff at recipients of Federal education funding (K-12 school districts, colleges, universities, and other educational institutions)
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX notice and training compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and publishing a recipient's notice of nondiscrimination, and for designing and delivering required Title IX trainings (who to train, required topics, frequency, impartiality requirements, and accessibility/publication rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures apply to resolution of complaints made by students, employees, or other individuals who are participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies §106.8(b)(2): grievance procedures are not limited to employee complaints; whether a postdoctoral trainee is an employee is fact-specific but they likely may make a complaint if participating or attempting to participate. See final §§106.2 (definition of 'complainant'), 106.8(b)(2), 106.45(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: No exhaustion requirement before filing with OCR
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX does not require a complainant to exhaust administrative remedies with a recipient prior to filing a complaint with the Office for Civil Rights (OCR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include a claim in the notice of nondiscrimination that individuals must exhaust internal remedies before contacting OCR; §106.8(c)(1)(i)(B) already clarifies inquiries may be referred to the recipient's Title IX Coordinator, OCR, or both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of training not required in notice
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is not required to include proof of Title IX training in its notice of nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients remain subject to training requirements under §106.8(d), but requiring proof in the notice would impose frequent updating burdens; thus the Department declines to require proof in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'attempting to participate' is broad
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'attempting to participate' (in §106.8(b)(2)) should be used rather than 'applying' because it better encompasses the broad circumstances in which a person might try to access a recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes applicants who withdrew but indicate desire to re-enroll if the recipient appropriately responds to sex-based harassment; the word 'applying' would inappropriately narrow application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice must identify where to find nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of nondiscrimination must include information on how to locate the recipient's nondiscrimination policy (§106.8(b)(1)) and the recipient's grievance procedures (§106.8(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations consolidate these requirements into §106.8(c)(1)(i)(D) and (E). The Department removed redundant citations to §§106.45 and 106.46 in that paragraph to avoid redundancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional disclosure of exemptions (including religious)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may, but is not required to, include information about any exceptions or exemptions (e.g., religious exemption) applicable under Title IX in its notice of nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice should limit its application to obligations 'required by Title IX and this part' to recognize statutory/regulatory exceptions. Requiring disclosure of religious exemptions would be impractical due to fact-specific intersections with religious tenets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication venues for notice of nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must publish its notice of nondiscrimination in its handbooks, catalogs, announcements, bulletins, application forms, and on its website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restores longstanding pre-2020 requirement (see §106.8(c)(2)). Recipients may include the notice in the same manner those materials are made available (print if distributed in print; electronically if only electronically maintained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-form notice allowed for space/format limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: If space/format limitations make full notice impracticable, a recipient may provide a shorter version of the notice (short-form) in printed materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-form may be a one-sentence statement that the recipient prohibits sex discrimination and that individuals may report concerns to the Title IX Coordinator, plus a link to the full notice on the website. See §106.8(c)(2)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in additional publication methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations do not bar a recipient from additionally posting the notice in public locations, sharing it at specific events, or re-distributing it annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may identify other ways, beyond the website or short-form, to provide access to the full notice if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility obligations (LEP and disability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must ensure meaningful access to the notice for individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP) and people with disabilities, though Title IX does not restate obligations under other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department emphasizes recipients remain responsible to comply with other Federal laws (e.g., Title VI, Section 504) that address accessibility; Title IX's publication requirement includes print and web posting to increase access for those without internet access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required training topics for all employees
rubrics_metrics.description: All employees must be trained on the recipient's obligation to address sex discrimination, the scope of conduct that constitutes sex discrimination (including the definition of 'sex-based harassment'), and applicable notification/information requirements under §§106.40(b)(2) and 106.44.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is specified in §106.8(d)(1). Training ensures all employees understand when and how to respond to potential sex discrimination under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required training topics for investigators/decisionmakers/others implementing grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators, decisionmakers, and other persons responsible for implementing the grievance procedures or with authority to modify/terminate supportive measures must be trained on obligations under §106.44, the recipient's grievance procedures under §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable); how to serve impartially (avoid prejudgment, conflicts of interest, bias); the meaning and application of 'relevant' for questions/evidence; and types of evidence impermissible regardless of relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is specified in §106.8(d)(2). Training should cover impartiality, relevance, and evidence rules to promote fair and lawful adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for informal resolution facilitators
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitators of the informal resolution process must be trained on the rules and practices associated with informal resolution and on serving impartially, including avoiding conflicts of interest and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified in §106.8(d)(3). Training supports fair and appropriate facilitation of informal resolution options under §106.44(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training for Title IX Coordinators and designees
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX Coordinators and their designees must be trained on their specific responsibilities under §§106.8(a), 106.40(b)(3), 106.44(f), 106.44(g); on the recipient's recordkeeping system and requirements under §106.8(f); and any other training necessary to coordinate Title IX compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Coordinators can fulfill coordination, recordkeeping, and procedural duties effectively and consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on trainings that rely on sex stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Training must not rely on sex stereotypes; trainings must address impartiality and avoiding bias and conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.8(d) specifically states trainings must not rely on sex stereotypes. The Department expects training materials and trainers to operate without bias; OCR can address biases identified in investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training frequency and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals identified as requiring training under §106.8(d) must receive training promptly upon hiring or upon a change of position that alters their Title IX duties, and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revises prior ambiguity: prompt training upon hiring/change of duties and annual retraining preserves flexibility while ensuring up-to-date knowledge. See revised §106.8(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to train all employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.8(d)(1) requires a recipient to train all employees (not merely make training available), and to train all personnel directly involved in carrying out Title IX duties in a manner that promotes compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes advisors, graduate students, contractors, volunteers, or third-party agents who are performing roles directly involved in Title IX duties; recipients need not train non-employees not directly involved but may choose to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in how to meet training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not prescribe specific training techniques, practices, or require hiring outside trainers; recipients have flexibility to structure and staff training to meet §106.8(d) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declines to require particular training practices beyond mandated topics (impartiality, conflicts, bias, relevance, impermissible evidence). Institutions can select best practices (e.g., trauma-informed practices) consistent with legal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of training materials for public inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must make training materials available for public inspection upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides public accountability and transparency as required by §106.8(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be free from bias and permit remedy for conflicts of interest or bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably; any person designated as Title IX Coordinator, investigator, decisionmaker, or facilitator must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual party; appeals must be offered if such bias/conflict is alleged and would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple provisions enforce impartiality (e.g., §§106.44(f)(1)(i), 106.45(b)(1), 106.44(k)(4), 106.45(b)(2), 106.46(i)(1)(iii)). Training is an important component but additional procedural protections are required.
